A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high tidal volume mechanical ventilator (TV) ventilation causes significant pulmonary inflammatory response in piglets.
the production of cytokines in BAL fluid increased in the group of pigs ventilated with high TV and that this increase was associated with increased concentrations of nitrites/nitratos and iNOS.
the mechanical stress caused by mechanical ventilation leads to an increase of inflammatory cytokines in bronchoalveloar lavage (BAL) in a piglet model of acute lung injury (ALI).
The main takeaway from our work is that
high TV mechanical ventilation is a strong inflammatory stimulus in piglets.
mechanical ventilation with a high tidal volume and low positive end-expiratory pressure is associated with an increase in proinflammatory cytokines and nitric oxide in piglet lungs.

mechanical ventilation with high tidal volumes (15 mL/kg) and low positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP = 0 cm H2O) is associated with increased production of cytokines and nitrites/nitrate in the lungs of pigs.
